$about: The size system of the site: every fluid size comes from this file. build/tokens.mjs reads it (npm run tokens, and before every dev/build), writes each size's value at every Figma Breakpoint mode into design/tokens.json (so Figma gets the same numbers) and one CSS formula per size into src/styles/base/tokens.gen.css. Explained with charts in design/README.md.

One range for everything: a size has its 'from' value on a 320px screen and its 'to' value on a 1440px one, and goes in a straight line in between (constant outside). Not the screen's width alone: a screen counts as only as big as its height allows (range.height): a screen 360px tall gets the sizes of a 320 screen, one 920px tall the sizes of a 1440 screen, a straight line in between (so every px of height a screen lacks counts as two px of width). A phone turned sideways gets the phone sizes, a 1366 × 650 laptop window the sizes of a 900 screen, and every size shrinks together.
One ladder for every size, type and space alike (ladder): steps of 2px up to 24, of 4px up to 64, of 8px up to 128. Both ends of every role are on it, so no size ends on an odd value like 36.6 or 31.

Type: a role is two sizes from the ladder, at 320 and at 1440. The roles keep their order and their distance at both ends: every pair in type.relations is at least type.relations.min apart (×1.125) on a 320 screen and on a 1440 one, and so at every size in between (the ratio of two straight lines can only move from its value at one end to its value at the other). Labels ("label": true) are set apart by case and weight, not size, and are left out of that.

Space: every spacing and radius is two numbers from the ladder (its value at 320 and at 1440). Roles marked size are measures of a block, not spacing, and need not be on the ladder. A role with "per" follows the width of its own block instead of the screen (per.from → per.to px of that width): the padding of a card that is narrow on a phone and wide on a tablet. A role with "by": "width" follows the screen's width alone, not its height.
Sizes are written in rem in the CSS (type) or px with the range in rem (space): with the browser's text made bigger, the whole system behaves as on a narrower screen, like the em steps of media.css.

type/hero.use: the hero title (60 at most: Tim, Oct 22)

type/h2.use: section headings, the CTA title, the titles of the card stack

type/card-heading.use: titles of cards: tools, publications, royalty; the 404 title

type/doc-title.use: the title of the legal documents (Tim, Oct 24)

type/lead.use: the text under the hero and the CTA titles

type/card-tag.use: the labels of the card stack: a label, set apart by uppercase, weight and its pill, not by size

type/body-m.use: the text of the tool cards

type/body.use: running text: publications, buttons, the footer

type/body-s.use: short text in small cards: the features, the bylines of the publications

type/ui.use: navbar links and button, menu, skip link, footer notes

type/note.use: the cookie notice: a note in the corner, below the UI size (12 everywhere)

relations.$about: Neighbouring levels that must stay apart at both ends of the range. Not here, on purpose: lead and body are the same on phones (16) and apart on computers (20 / 16); body-m, body and body-s are one text size on phones and differ by 2px on computers.

aliases.$about: Figma variables the text styles still use, now the same as a role (the site uses only the roles)

section/pad-x.use: side gutter of every section: the content column starts here

stack/pad.use: inset of the full-bleed cards (stack, CTA) from the screen edge, and the gap between stack cards; the hero is the screen less twice this

section/pad-y.use: space above and below a section's content (two sections in a row: twice this between them)

section/gap.use: from a section heading to its content

section/air-l.use: more air: under the CTA card; above and below the tools and the publications, and from their headings to their cards (Tim, Oct 20)

space/gap-tiles.use: between tiles: features, logos and stats

radius/s.use: tiles: features, logos, stats (about 130–250px wide); 32 at most (Tim, Oct 22)

radius/m.use: half-column cards: publications, royalty; the padding of the stack cards; the side padding of the CTA card

radius/l.use: full-column cards: the CTA card, tool cards

cta/air.use: above and below the content of the CTA card (at least): generous at every size

space/pad-l.use: the air under the text of a tool card, above its picture (when they stand one under the other)

tool/pad.use: padding of the tool cards, by the card's own width across the whole column: 28px on a 288px card (a 320 phone), about 35 on a 430px one (a 480 phone), 48 on a 700px one (a 768 window), 64 on the widest, 1024px (Tim, Oct 24: it shrinks with the screen at every size; design/decisions.json)

card/text-pad.use: padding of a stack card (= radius/m)

card/text-gap.use: a stack card's label → its title

space/text-gap.use: a heading → its text: hero, CTA, tools, publications

space/action-gap.use: a block of text → its button: hero, CTA

tool/gap.use: a tool card's text → its button

feature/gap.use: a feature's icon → its text (at least)

pub/air.use: a publication's text → its footer (at least)

hero/air-top.use: under the navbar, above the hero title (at least: the hero is taller than the screen rather than less)

hero/air-bottom.use: under the hero button, above the team (at least)

hero/air-max.use: above and below the hero's text at most: the hero stops growing there, on tall screens

hero/pic-min.use: the least height of the team at the table (by the screen's width only: a short laptop keeps a big picture; never more than the picture's height for the width)

hero/text.use: about how tall the hero's text is (title, lead, button): only for the hero's greatest height

space/center-air.use: air at the sides of a centred heading, so a line of big letters is not pressed against the gutter on phones

nav/pad-right.use: a little less than the left on phones: the burger's lines have air of their own

footer/contact-y.use: more air on phones, where the contacts stand in a column

tool/min-h.use: a tool card's least height when text and picture sit side by side, from step L (a 1024 window; Tim, Oct 24)
